description: This horizontal bar chart, from the paper “Are Large Language Models Really Good Logical Reasoners: A Comprehensive Evaluation and Beyond,” displays the percentage of matched responses for six distinct categories, with each bar representing the proportion of “Matched” (solid blue) and “Not Matched” (light blue) outcomes. The vertical axis lists the categories in descending order of their total matched percentage: “No Hallucination,” “Oriented,” “Active,” “Correct,” “Rigorous,” and “Active.” The horizontal axis represents the percentage scale, ranging from 0% to 100%, with tick marks at 20% intervals. Each bar is segmented to show the contribution of “Matched” and “Not Matched” results, with the “Matched” portion labeled with its percentage value (e.g., “No Hallucination” is 98.33% matched, “Correct” is 99.00% matched) and the “Not Matched” portion labeled with its percentage of the total bar length (e.g., “No Hallucination” is 1.67% not matched, “Correct” is 1.00% not matched). The “Matched” portion is consistently represented by a solid blue bar, while the “Not Matched” portion is represented by a light blue segment, and a legend in the lower center confirms this color coding. The bars are sorted in descending order based on the total matched percentage, with “Correct” (99.00%) being the highest and “No Hallucination” (98.33%) being the second highest. The chart does not show any bars that are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or outlines.
